tests.name: Thumb extension test
tests.setting: Patients presenting with non-traumatic wrist pain to a tertiary care clinic; 48 with TMC arthritis, 44 with radial sided wrist and hand pain, and 47 with other wrist pain. Mean age 52 years, 67% female.
tests.comment: The examiner places ipsilateral thumb along radial aspect of patients distal thumb metacarpal, 5 to 10 mm proximal to the thumb MCP joint, and extends the thumb until the thumb metacarpal is in a plane parallel to the palm. Pain at TMC joint is a positive test

tests.name: Thumb adduction test
tests.setting: Patients presenting with non-traumatic wrist pain to a tertiary care clinic; 48 with TMC arthritis, 44 with radial sided wrist and hand pain, and 47 with other wrist pain. Mean age 52 years, 67% female.
tests.comment: The examiner places ipsilateral hand so thumb rests dorsally over the head of the patient's thumb metacarpal, with the ulnar side of the patients wrist supported by the examiner's other hand. The examiner firmly pushes downward on the patient's thumb metacarpal; pain at the TMC joint is a positive test.

tests.name: Liftoff test
tests.setting: Consecutive adutls undergoing arthroscopic surgery for suspected rotator cuff tear.
tests.comment: Place dorsum of patient's hand on patient's back at mi-lumbar spine. Patient asked to rotate arm internally so as to lift the hand posteriorly off his or her back. Positive if unable to lift hand.

tests.name: Bear hug test
tests.setting: Consecutive adutls undergoing arthroscopic surgery for suspected rotator cuff tear.
tests.comment: Palm of involved side placed on opposite shoulder with fingers extended and elbow positioned anterior to the body. Patient is then asked to hold that position as the examiner tries to pull their hand away from their shoulder with an external rotation forced applied perpendicularly to the forearm. Positive if patient could not hold their hand against their shoulder.

tests.name: Napoleon test
tests.setting: Consecutive adutls undergoing arthroscopic surgery for suspected rotator cuff tear.
tests.comment: Palm of the hand on the involved side is placed on his or her belly in supine position. Examiner holds patient's hand and shoulder fixed to prevent compensatory motion. Patient is asked to move his or her elbow upward away from exam table. Test is positive if patient could not lift his or her elbow off the table or if distance between elbow and table is < 5 cm (2 inches).

tests.name: Anterior slide test
tests.setting: Consecutive patients presenting with shoulder pain for arthroscopy.
tests.comment: AST: Arm positioned with hand on ipsilateral hip and thumb pointing posteriorly. Stabilize shoulder and acromion and use other hand to place anterior and superiorly directed axial load on humerus. Pain and/or click is positive. Data collection standardized, but analysis retrospective. Probably not blinded.

tests.name: Passive distraction test
tests.setting: Consecutive patients presenting with shoulder pain for arthroscopy.
tests.comment: PDT: Patient supin, elevate arm to 150 in coronal plane with elbow extended and forearm supinated. Pronation = pain is positive test. Data collection standardized, but analysis retrospective. Probably not blinded.

tests.name: Active compression test
tests.setting: Consecutive patients presenting with shoulder pain for arthroscopy.
tests.comment: ACT: Arm forward flexed 90 with elbow fully extended, then adduct arm 10-15 medial to sagittal plane and internally rotate so thumb points down. Apply downward force. If pain present, and not present when palm facing up, positive test. Data collection standardized, but analysis retrospective. Probably not blinded.

tests.name: Passive distraction test + active compression test
tests.setting: Consecutive patients presenting with shoulder pain for arthroscopy.
tests.comment: Data collection standardized, but analysis retrospective. Probably not blinded.

tests.name: Yergason test
tests.setting: Prospective consecutive series of patients undergoing shoulder surgery for shoulder symptoms
tests.comment: With the patient’s elbow flexed to 90  and stabilized against the thorax; with the forearm pronated, the examiner resisted supination. A positive test result was indicated by pain localized to the bicipital groove

tests.name: Speed test
tests.setting: Prospective consecutive series of patients undergoing shoulder surgery for shoulder symptoms
tests.comment: The Speed test was performed by having the patient forward flex the shoulder to 90  with the elbow extended and the forearm supinated. Resistance was applied to the forearm, and a positive result was recorded if pain was localized to the bicipital groove.

tests.name: Upper cut test
tests.setting: Prospective consecutive series of patients undergoing shoulder surgery for shoulder symptoms
tests.comment: With the involved shoulder in a neutral position, the elbow flexed to 90 , the forearm supinated, and the patient making a fist. The patient was asked to rapidly bring the hand up and toward the chin. The examiner placed a hand over the patient’s fist and resisted the motion as the hand came up to the chin. A positive test result was pain or a painful pop over the anterior portion of the involved shoulder during the resisted movement.

tests.name: Tap test
tests.setting: Prospective blinded study of 70 limbs in 44 patients referred for surgical treatment of varicose veins.
tests.comment: Place hand on varicosities and tap on saphenofemoral junction (5 cm below/medial to femoral pulse). If venous reflux feel fluid thrill.

tests.name: Cough test
tests.setting: Prospective blinded study of 70 limbs in 44 patients referred for surgical treatment of varicose veins.
tests.comment: Palpate saphenofemoral opening 5 cm below/medial femoral pulse as patient stands and coughs. If reflux, cough creates fluid thrill.

tests.name: Trendelenberg test
tests.setting: Prospective blinded study of 70 limbs in 44 patients referred for surgical treatment of varicose veins.
tests.comment: Patient supine, leg elevated, tourniquet around thigh 5 cm below femoral pulse. When pt stands if normal valve will see blood slowly filling below tourniquet. If reflux will have suddent gush filling from above when touniquet removed.

tests.name: Perthes test
tests.setting: Prospective blinded study of 70 limbs in 44 patients referred for surgical treatment of varicose veins.
tests.comment: Patient standing, place tourniquet around mid-thigh, patient walks for 5 min. If saphenous veins collapse below tourniquet deep veins are patent and communicating veins are competent; if unchanged, both saphenous and communicating veins are incompetent.
